transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I used to be able to focus for hours on designs, but now my mind feels foggy and I can’t make even basic decisions at work. I transitioned to a demanding full-time engineering role about a year ago, and my manager recently suggested I seek help because of how much I've been struggling.

Did these problems start soon after the new engineering job or another major stress, or did they come on even without a clear trigger? Have they stayed tied to that stress, or do they persist regardless of what’s happening at work?

They started a few months after I transitioned into this full-time role about fourteen months ago, initially triggered by the intense workload and my demanding supervisor. But now, this heavy depression and foggy thinking have become a constant, daily weight. It persists every single day, regardless of how things are actually going at work.

Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or hopeless most of the day nearly every day, and have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? If yes, did these symptoms continue even during times when work stress was lighter or absent?

Yes, I've felt down and hopeless nearly every day, and this has actually been going on for over a year, not just the last two weeks. I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like tinkering with 3-D printers and running with my track club, and they now feel completely flat and pointless. These feelings persist constantly, even during the rare times when the stress at work is lighter.

Over the past two weeks, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, trouble concentrating, or feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt? If so, which of these have been happening nearly every day?

Yes, I’ve been dealing with almost all of those nearly every day for over a year now. My concentration is completely gone—my brain feels like static, and I struggle to make simple decisions or even read a basic drawing. I also feel like a complete fraud and lie awake at night replaying work mistakes, leaving me constantly exhausted.

Before this current period that started about a year ago, have you ever had another separate time in your life lasting at least 2 weeks when you felt similarly depressed and lost interest in things? Or is this the first episode like this?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is definitely the first time I've ever felt this depressed and lost, and it's completely new to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a first depressive episode lasting over a year with persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue, impaired concentration/indecisiveness, and worthlessness/guilt occurring nearly every day and persisting beyond fluctuations in work stress. There is clear occupational impairment. No prior depressive episodes were reported, supporting a single current major depressive episode. Based on the candidate set provided, the best-fitting ICD-10 diagnosis is severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
